item.title: Harvest Season for SLUB: From io_uring vulnerability to Novel Sheaf-Based Exploitation Techniques
item.description: Problem: A Linux SLUB allocator bug reachable via io_uring needs a reliable exploit. Approach: Per the title, the paper builds a novel exploitation technique around SLUB's 'sheaf' per-CPU caching structure. Result: Not verified — the arXiv page could not be fetched (403), so no details or numbers are available. Why it matters: Kernel allocator changes can open new exploit paths past existing hardening. Glossary: SLUB (Linux kernel heap allocator); io_uring (async I/O kernel interface); sheaf (SLUB per-CPU object cache).

item.title: New Spectre-v2 BTR Attack Leaks Linux Memory Despite Existing Defenses
item.description: Problem: Spectre-v2 defenses were meant to stop branch-prediction attacks on the Linux kernel. Approach: Per the headline, a new 'BTR' (Branch Target Reuse) variant leaks kernel memory despite current mitigations. Result: Not verified — the article could not be fetched (403); the headline reports Linux memory leakage. Why it matters: Mitigations may need rework, and patches matter on shared Linux hosts. Glossary: Spectre-v2 (branch target injection); speculative execution (CPU guessing ahead); BTR (branch target reuse).
